content.comment_body: Is the Latching Relay (RS) command able to retain its state in the older [product_name] processors? The newer processors provide a retentive setting on the block, but the older units did not. What was the default for the older processors? Thanks in advance.
Hello, Only the [article_no] did not support retentive RS. Since it's an RS, upon power loss the reset becomes the active state. Regards,
Thank you [user_name]. So, did the retentive option become available starting from the [article_no] version onward?
A quick check in the [product_name] software... YES – the [article_no] introduced the retentive selection. Why the question about its history?

Thanks [user_name]. I have a client using a [article_no] model that has failed and won't power on. I'm trying to transfer the program from the memory of this model to a [article_no] model. While doing this, I noticed the newer model offers options not found in the older unit, and the manuals were not clear about the original default setting for retentivity. Thanks again.
Wow! Replacing a [article_no] model only now is rare. If you set retain parameters to OFF for all blocks, you should have the original function. Thanks for the update.

For all [product_name] modules and [product_name] software, the default setting for retentivity is OFF. To enable retentivity, it must be set explicitly; if you don't set it, it's always OFF. Only the Hourcounter feature has retentivity that cannot be disabled.

Almost all versions, but the [article_no] model being discussed here has no retentivity at all. From [article_no] onward, that is correct. @ [user_name], my [product_name] [article_no] is still operating, running 24/7 to control a fan in the bathroom. Regards,

analysis.insight_summary: Users reviewed the retentivity settings for Latching Relay (RS) commands in earlier and later [product_name] models. The main takeaway is that the oldest release ([article_no]) had no retentive capability, while subsequent versions added it. By default, retentivity settings are OFF unless specified otherwise, and documentation did not clearly explain legacy model defaults, which complicates migration of programs between versions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect clear guidance about default retentivity configurations in both older and newer [product_name] models. This clarity is needed to facilitate the migration and correct functionality of control programs when switching between product versions.
